name: pam_unix
detailed_description: Traditional UNIX authentication module that uses standard system files (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/group) for user authentication. Selection of encryption methods are mutually exclusive, appropriate algorithm need to be verified for actual support. Supports password encryption with various methods including MD5, SHA512, and crypt. This is the fundamental building block of most PAM configurations and typically serves as the first authentication method.

[Without]algorithm.bigcrypt: (deprecated) and weak implementation of DES C2
[Without]algorithm.blowfish: (obsolete) use bcrypt encryption, limited to 72 characters
[Without]algorithm.scrypt: (experimental) use of scrypt slow hash funcition
[Without]algorithm.yescrypt: Use of yescrypt slow hash function (recommended)
[Without]algorithm.argon2id: (experimental) use of Argon2id slow hash function
[Without]algorithm.gost_yescrypt: Use yescrypt with Streebog (glitch in Streebog found in 2015)
[Without]algorithm.sm3-yescrypt: (experimental) Chinese standard based on SM3 hash function

notes:
Most basic authentication module, typically foundation of PAM stack
